bullets.title: NVDA: MS reinstates as Top Pick, $300 PT; Feynman architecture targets >$50B revenue/GW
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley reinstated NVDA as Top Pick (Overweight, $300 PT ~20x CY27 EPS) after a constructive NDR, citing a broader customer base than assumed (~50% ACIE segment), Vera Rubin ramp, and Feynman (2028) lifting revenue/GW from $40B to >$50B. FY28 revenue guide of +70% y/y is supply-constrained with demand closer to 100%; stock at ~15x FY28 EPS seen as undemanding. Hedgeye also remains long NVDA as a core mega-cap position.

bullets.title: STX/WDC: Toshiba HDD capacity scare — Citi and MS say buy the dip
bullets.body: Toshiba announced plans to double HDD production capacity by FY27 with ~$380M capex, sending STX -11% and WDC -7.5% to -13.8% pre-market. Citi maintains Buy on both (STX $1,300 PT, WDC $740 PT at 23x FY28 EPS), arguing Toshiba's lack of internal media/heads supply limits total EB impact to ~200bps of EB shipment CAGR; supply-demand gap remains >300 EB with capacity sold through CY28. MS echoes the dip-buy call; Klein's desk flags VECO as a derivative buy as dominant ion-beam tool supplier for HDD capex.

bullets.title: LITE/COHR: FCC optical transceiver restrictions on China seen as major tailwind
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley and JPM both flagged that DC meetings indicate the FCC is likely to restrict Chinese optical transceiver suppliers starting at the 3.2T generation (2028+ ramp), directly benefiting US laser vendors LITE and COHR. COHR surged +10.9%, LITE +7.7%, and FN +6.4% on the session. MS explicitly identifies LITE and COHR as buy on this regulatory catalyst.

bullets.title: AAPL: iPhone Duo yield issues, Vision Pro pushed to 2028/29, CEO reorganization risk
bullets.body: New Apple CEO reorganization is creating higher execution risk with faster development cycles and departures from traditional launch cadences. iPhone Duo assembly yields were ~60% in mid-September and could take 6-12 months to normalize, limiting supply. Vision Pro lacks product-market fit and has been pushed to late 2028/early 2029, with the Vision team described as on 'life support.' Hedgeye remains long AAPL as a core position.

bullets.title: META: $300 PT bull thesis intact; Muse agent and $40B penalty exposure are key debates
bullets.body: Hedgeye flags META alongside MSFT as the 'alpha dogs' in mega-caps. JPM's Chips for Breakfast note suggests META could be positioned as 'aggregator of aggregators' via Muse with structural trust advantages vs. vertical agents, potentially keeping Muse ad-free while monetizing through Facebook/Instagram. Countervailing risk: New Mexico jury found META misled consumers on data privacy — company faces up to $40B in penalties (disputes figure, says max is $3.45B).

bullets.title: MSFT: JPM hosting Oct 6 Copilot/M365 distribution partner webinar; bullish AI thesis intact
bullets.body: JPM is hosting a webinar on Oct 6 with TD SYNNEX global distribution partner to discuss Microsoft's Copilot and M365 application suite. Buyside desk notes MSFT OpenAI acceleration should drive Azure AI outperformance into year-end; Hedgeye identifies MSFT as the strongest mega-cap alpha alongside META.

bullets.title: AMD: +289.9% YTD, hitting 52-week high at $639.50; semis broadly surging post-payrolls
bullets.body: AMD touched $639.50 (+3.9% intraday) on Oct 2, representing a 52-week gain of +289.9% — the top YTD performer among large-cap tech at a new 52-week high. The broader semiconductor complex (SOXX +2.46%) rallied post soft payrolls: ARM +5.0%, MRVL +3.4%, INTC +3.0%, MTSI +3.1%, TXN +2.7%.

bullets.title: APP: At 52-week low (-61.3% YTD); loses TRO vs Unity in data dispute
bullets.body: AppLovin hit a 52-week low at $272.70 (-3.1% intraday, -61.3% YTD). A judge denied APP's temporary restraining order against Unity (U) over a data collection dispute; U is receiving more positive buyside checks vs. APP's negative reads per Citi.

bullets.title: NFLX: MS sees double-digit revenue growth, ~200bps margin expansion; 3Q preview bullish
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley maintains optimism on NFLX despite investor sentiment souring toward YouTube, flagging double-digit revenue growth potential and ~200bps margin expansion with India as a new growth bright spot. Citi's 3Q26 preview expects NFLX to report slightly above guidance with better video game engagement. Citi flags NFLX as a 'call for info' into the print.

bullets.title: SHOP: MS flags as 'agnostic Agentic shopping winner'; Canvas AI tool launched
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley positions Shopify as an agnostic winner in the agentic AI commerce shift given its transaction-based model; the company recently launched Canvas, an AI store-builder tool. SHOP was up +2.2% in Canadian pre-market trading (C$216.74).

bullets.title: TSLA: Q3 deliveries 486,532 beat consensus 463,761; memory de-spec on AI hardware
bullets.body: Tesla delivered 486,532 vehicles in Q3 (consensus 463,761), above expectations, though energy storage deployments of 13.7 GW missed consensus 15.3 GW (described as lumpy). On the AI hardware side, MS flags TSLA cut AI5 memory specs 50% to 72GB LPDDR5 and AI6 by one-third to 144GB LPDDR6 to secure Optimus production volume — a modest negative read-through for memory suppliers.

bullets.title: MU: Bullish on trade and trend; $30B+ quarterly buyback starting December seen as key re-rate catalyst
bullets.body: Hedgeye recommends buying dips in MU. Buyside desk notes MU feedback is muted with no immediate re-rate expected despite a strong recent print, but a $30B+ quarterly buyback program starting in December is flagged as the key potential catalyst. MU commentary lifted the memory sector +3.0% on the day.

bullets.title: HPE: Daiwa upgrades to Outperform, raises PT to $75; stock +5.8% intraday
bullets.body: Daiwa (analyst Louis Miscioscia) upgraded Hewlett Packard Enterprise to Outperform from Neutral and raised its price target to $75 from $65, implying ~9% upside from current levels. HPE traded at $68.40 (+5.8% intraday), a 52-week gain of +174.2%. FactSet consensus target is $73.11.

bullets.title: DDOG: FBN Securities initiates Outperform with $325 PT (17% upside)
bullets.body: FBN Securities initiated coverage of Datadog with an Outperform rating and $325 price target, implying 17% upside from $278.70. The FactSet consensus target is $289.09 with a range of $158–$340.

bullets.title: PSKY/WBD: Ticker changes to SKYD Oct 6; PSKY-WBD merger closes same day
bullets.body: Paramount Skydance will change its ticker from PSKY to SKYD and list Class B common stock on NYSE effective Oct 6, 2026, coinciding with the anticipated close of the Warner Bros. Discovery merger. The company will also be renamed Skydance Corporation; warrant record date is Oct 5.

bullets.title: CRWV: JPM hosting joint equity & credit call Oct 7 on business fundamentals and capital structure
bullets.body: JPMorgan is organizing a joint equity and credit research discussion on CoreWeave on Wednesday, Oct 7 at 10am ET, covering business fundamentals and capital structure/credit market access implications. Separately, JPM's Chips for Breakfast note flags CRWV as vulnerable once customer contracts expire.

bullets.title: TMUS: Citi Neutral; solid 3Q expected, 4Q upside from pricing, but LEO/structure overhangs persist
bullets.body: Citi maintains Neutral on T-Mobile, expecting generally in-line 3Q results with potential upward bias in 4Q from incremental pricing actions (fee increases of $1.00/line/month for voice effective Oct 12). Market focus remains on LEO competition in mobile, spectrum investments, corporate structure uncertainty, and AI agent impacts on ARPUs, limiting near-term sentiment improvement.

bullets.title: VST: Initiated Buy at Siebert Williams Shank, $202 PT; TLN led utilities higher
bullets.body: Vistra Energy was initiated with a Buy rating and $202 price target at Siebert Williams Shank (below FactSet consensus of $216). TLN led the electric utilities group higher the prior session. EIX was downgraded to Underperform at Jefferies (PT cut to $42 from $53) on SoCalEd criminal probe liability risk not priced in.

bullets.title: GLW: AT&T signs $3B+ multi-year fiber supply deal; Display segment faces 2027 demand headwinds
bullets.body: Corning secured a $3B+ multi-year fiber supply agreement with AT&T, a positive for the optical fiber business. However, JPM's Chips for Breakfast flags GLW's Display segment under pressure from elevated memory costs (3x higher in 3Q26 vs. year-ago), with TV makers reluctant to commit to aggressive 2027 purchases.

bullets.title: DKNG: Hedgeye hosting online gaming reset; downward GGR TAM revision expected, SCOTUS prediction market risk flagged
bullets.body: Hedgeye is hosting an online gaming reset presentation covering DKNG, FLUT, and RSI, with downward revisions expected to long-term GGR TAMs/SAMs through 2030. Growing doubt about recent handle acceleration matching hold and promo performance, and a SCOTUS showdown on prediction markets flagged as a potential structural risk to the sector.
